description:
Two CSV files containing quarterly US macroeconomic data from the Federal Reserve (FRED) have been placed in /home/ga/Documents/gretl_data/: 'PCEC96.csv' (Real Personal Consumption Expenditures, billions of chained 2017 dollars) and 'DSPIC96.csv' (Real Disposable Personal Income, billions of chained 2017 dollars), both quarterly from 1947Q1 to present.

A macroeconomist needs to test the permanent income hypothesis: that consumption and income are cointegrated. Your task:
1. Import both CSV files into Gretl and create time-series variables
2. Apply log transformation to both series (lcons = log(PCEC96), linc = log(DSPIC96))
3. Test each series for unit roots using the Augmented Dickey-Fuller (ADF) test (both level and first-difference)
4. Test for cointegration between lcons and linc using the Engle-Granger two-step method
5. Estimate the long-run relationship (cointegrating regression) and save the residuals
6. Test the residuals for stationarity (ADF on residuals — the cointegration test)
7. Save all results to /home/ga/Documents/gretl_output/cointegration_results.txt

Gretl is running and the FRED data files are available at the specified paths.

metadata.data_source: US Bureau of Economic Analysis via FRED (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis)
